chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the employment (of wet-nurses) of the Magian, so he said: No, but (the wet-nurses of) the People of the Book.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to employ a Magian as a wet-nurse for a child?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the Magians (Zoroastrians) and the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) regarding the permissibility of employing them as wet-nurses. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while Magians are considered a distinct group with their own purity laws, the People of the Book are generally treated similarly to Muslims in matters of social interaction and consumption, provided they are not polytheists.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kahily, from Abdullah Bin Hilal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about (employing) the wet-nurses of the Magians. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but the People of the Book’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahiliy from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Hilal who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if a Zoroastrian woman can be hired for breastfeeding a child. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, however, she can be of the people of the book.’”
